declaration.reason: Owner-authorised 24 November 2026 meeting governance change for meeting-specific Chairperson, Secretary and Meeting Administrator appointments; temporary Transition Committee election workflow; server-enforced role separation; meeting-scoped invitations, ballots and media moderation; and immediate Transition Committee mandate expiry when formal proceedings begin. This change explicitly includes the necessary meeting-scoped Firestore authorization rules; no unrelated collection, portal or signature rules are changed.
declaration.expectedEffect: Allow active registered IRPA members and employees to initiate meetings; permit initial registration with no permanent leadership appointments; require a complete temporary Transition Committee before leadership-election invitations and ballots; allow eligible participants to vote only in that election; require all three permanent meeting appointments and closed election ballots before proceedings; expire temporary authority atomically at proceedings start; keep Meeting Administrator authority operational only; preserve Board-only quorum, voting, resolutions, signature and record protections. The legacy Firebase LiveKit callable is also hardened so only the meeting-specific Meeting Administrator can receive room moderation or control recording; global administrators, initiators, Chairpersons and Secretaries cannot obtain technical moderation by legacy callable paths. The Voting Process page now opens and closes ballots through the meeting Worker using the current meeting's Chairperson/Secretary or active Transition Committee Chairperson/Secretary; global administrator status alone does not confer voting control. Ordinary governance votes remain Board-member-only, while pre-proceedings leadership-election ballots admit listed active members and employees.
prohibitedChanges: Do not create portal-wide meeting leadership roles.
Do not allow Meeting Administrator to chair, vote, establish quorum, approve resolutions or approve minutes by virtue of that role.
Do not retain Transition Committee authority after formal proceedings begin.
Do not allow appointments or permissions to leak between concurrent meetings.
Do not weaken Board quorum, ordinary governance voting, signature, legal-hold, retention, audit or protected deletion safeguards.
Do not change unrelated Firestore collections or other portal permissions.
